title: Spare harmonicas and harmonica keys in his concertos
summary: He carries spares, and describes which harmonica keys he uses in each movement of both concertos.

blocks.x: I was wondering, I don't know why this occurred to me but there’s a, you know a nice video of you with your, playing your concerto, I think it’s with the Evanston Symphony.
I wondered, does he have a spare harmonica in his pocket?

Oh, yeah. Because I mean that’s why I carry, I usually carry like two or three in the keys that I use the most because sometimes they’ll get clogged up or something will happen to it and so I can always reach over and grab another one. That particular concerto I compose it for – each movement is using a different key harmonica, for whatever reason I decided to do that. First movement uses a G, second movement an A, and the third movement a C. My new concerto that I just, that I’m going to premier in February, this one, it’s called – I still forget the name of the damn thing – “Eastern European Harmonica and Piano Concerto for Single Soloist.” This one I use a B flat harmonica for almost the whole piece except for the second movement because I like the B flat harmonica. And the second movement I do a bunch of simultaneous piano and harmonica playing and since the G harp is the first one I learned on, I see the G harp the most directly as a piano keyboard. So when I’m playing those things together usually I’m using a G harp.
